name: emoji-picker

frames.best_why: Full picker with search, category tabs, a dense emoji grid and the preview footer all visible.

tagline: Searchable emoji grid in a compact popover with a preview footer.
summary: A compact emoji picker with a search box, a row of category tabs, a scrollable grid of native emoji and a footer preview. Typing filters by name or shortcode, and picking one writes it to the linked field.
appearance: A narrow dark rounded panel with a pill search field on top, then a row of small grey category icons, a caption for the current category and a dense six-column grid of yellow emoji. A footer strip shows a larger emoji with its name and shortcode and a small hand icon at the right.
behaviour: Typing in the search filters the grid live and switches the heading to Search results, while a clear button empties it. Hovering an emoji updates the footer preview, and clicking one selects it and writes its value to the field below the panel.
demo_content: Search terms 'rd' and 'rocket'; smiley, flag and food emoji; and the status line 'Status for #design-crit'.
search_phrases: insert a reaction into a message
pick a face for a comment
use_when: Users need to drop an emoji into a chat, comment or status field and want search and categories, not a long scroll.
avoid_when: It fetches its emoji data from a CDN by default, so it needs network access or a self-hosted data URL.
customise: Locale, data URL or bundled data, shortcode presets, labels, skin tone, custom emoji and categories, multi-select and recents are options; styling comes from CSS variables.
weight_why: Fetches a large emoji dataset and renders a virtualized grid; heavier than it looks.

a11y.note: Search, categories and the grid are labelled and keyboard-driven with a polite live region; reduced motion is not explicitly detected.

issues: The six-column emoji grid is dense and small, so rows are hard to scan at this width.
The category tabs and clear button are tiny icon-only controls with no visible labels.
polish_why: Compact picker with a clear preview; the dense grid and tiny icon tabs are hard to read.
